observation.evaluation:
Correctness: PARTIALLY_CORRECT
Safety: CAUTION
Issues: Single lateral radiograph cannot reliably lateralize a pleural effusion — the posterior costophrenic angles of both hemidiaphragms are superimposed; the prominent "L" marker denotes the patient's left side nearest the detector (projection/orientation marker), not which hemithorax contains the effusion; posterior costophrenic blunting is suggested but laterality (right vs left) cannot be confirmed without a frontal PA/AP view or the source report.
Suggestion: Correlate with a frontal (PA/AP) chest radiograph or the original radiology report to confirm right versus left before finalizing; if only this lateral image is available, state the laterality as indeterminate rather than asserting right pleural effusion.
